userStories.title: Approval gate takes a minimum mode
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add a contextual minimum approval mode to the engine and REST route gate without lowering existing policy or multi-key requirements.

**Motivation** — The permission redesign (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-18-permission-approval-redesign-design.md`, "Shipped defaults") lists the self-fix rule; no code implements it.

**Approach** — `ApprovalGate.gate` and `RouteGateCall` take an optional `minMode: ApprovalMode`. The gate composes in this order:
1. resolve the primary key and every `alsoKeys` key, and keep the strictest resolution (unchanged, #384);
2. if `minMode` is present, the kept resolution's `source` is not `'not-approvable'`, and `minMode` is stricter than its mode, replace it with `{ mode: minMode, floor: <the kept resolution's floor>, policy: null, source: 'default' }`.
Step 2 never lowers a mode and never applies to a non-approvable key. Replacing the policy with `null` means a request opened only because of `minMode` uses the no-policy defaults (`onTimeout: 'reject'`, timeout `DEFAULT_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_SEC`, `approverMustHoldAction: true`, `requireDistinctApprover: false`), so a policy that allows auto-approve on timeout cannot release it. The rest of the gate is unchanged: `none` executes, a USER subject executes with `satisfiedBy: 'human'`, any other subject gets a pending request whose `requiredMode` is the final mode. `ApprovalRouteGate.run` forwards `minMode` only when the call carries it.

**Scope** — In: gate option composition, RouteGateCall and conditional forwarding, existing gate and route-gate unit specs. Out: the ticket identity lookup (US-002), ticket route floors (US-003), credential tiers and CI route floor (US-004); no catalog-wide permanent floor is introduced.

**Interface** — Target gate options: `opts: { projectId: string | null; variant?: string; alsoKeys?: readonly string[]; minMode?: ApprovalMode }`. `RouteGateCall` gains `minMode?: ApprovalMode`. Read `APPROVAL_MODE_RANK`, `modeAtLeast`, `strictestMode` and `ResolvedApproval = { mode, floor, policy, source }` without changing their contracts. Preserve exact option objects for calls that omit `minMode`.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] ApprovalGate.gate for an AGENT actor, with the resolver answering mode 'none' (source 'default') for the key and opts.minMode 'agent', returns status 'pending' with an opened request whose requiredMode is 'agent'.
[unit] When the resolver answers mode 'self' from a policy with onTimeout 'approve' and opts.minMode is 'agent', the opened request has { policyId: null, onTimeout: 'reject' }.
[unit] ApprovalGate.gate executes the command and returns status 'executed' with approval.requiredMode 'none' for the first case without minMode, preserving the existing no-minimum path.
[unit] When the resolver answers 'human' from policy id 'p-1' and opts.minMode is 'agent', the opened request has { requiredMode: 'human', policyId: 'p-1' }.

[unit] For a USER actor with resolver mode 'none' and opts.minMode 'agent', the command executes with outcome approval { requiredMode: 'agent', satisfiedBy: 'human', approverType: 'USER', approverId: <the user's id> }.
[unit] With alsoKeys ['k2'], primary mode 'none', k2 mode 'self' and opts.minMode 'agent', the opened request's requiredMode is 'agent'.
[unit] With alsoKeys ['k2'], primary mode 'none', k2 mode 'human' and opts.minMode 'agent', the opened request's requiredMode is 'human'.
[unit] With resolver mode 'none', source 'not-approvable' and opts.minMode 'agent', ApprovalGate.gate executes the command without opening a request.
[unit] ApprovalRouteGate.run({ key, variant, projectId, input, minMode: 'agent' }) calls gate.gate once with opts.minMode 'agent'.
[unit] ApprovalRouteGate.run without minMode calls gate.gate with an opts object that has no minMode property.

When minMode raises a policy resolution, the opened request uses DEFAULT_APPROVAL_TIMEOUT_SEC, approverMustHoldAction true and requireDistinctApprover false.

userStories.title: The ticket service answers the self-fix approval floor
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Resolve the latest VERIFY_FIX actor and return a contextual agent approval floor only when that actor is the current caller.

**Motivation** — The Developer role holds `ticket.transition.*`, so a Developer agent closes its own ticket on a self-written review, and the audit records `requiredMode: none`.

**Approach** — `ITicketRepository.findLatestStatusChangeActor(ticketId, toStatus)` reads the newest `TicketActivity` row with `action = 'STATUS_CHANGE'` and that `toStatus` (order `createdAt` desc, then `id` desc) and answers `{ type: 'AGENT', id: actorAgentId }` when `actorAgentId` is set, else `{ type: 'USER', id: actorUserId }` when that is set, else `null`; no row answers `null`. `TicketsService.selfFixApprovalFloor(projectSlug, ref, principal): Promise<'agent' | undefined>` loads the ticket the way `findByRef` does (same 404s). It answers `undefined` without reading activity when the ticket's status is not `VERIFY_FIX`. Otherwise it reads the latest `VERIFY_FIX` actor and answers `'agent'` when that actor's `type` equals the caller's kind (`principal.actorType` `'user'` -> `'USER'`, `'agent'` -> `'AGENT'`) and its `id` equals `principal.id`, else `undefined`; a `'runner'` principal (never reaches these routes) answers `undefined`.

**Scope** — In: repository interface and single-query implementation, scoped service lookup, existing service unit fixtures and new real-DB repository cases. Out: gate minimum-mode composition (US-001), consuming route changes (US-003), PR-link query (US-006). A fix actor recorded as neither a user nor an agent (a system writer) never matches a caller.

**Interface**
```typescript
findLatestStatusChangeActor(ticketId: string, toStatus: TicketStatus): Promise<{ type: 'USER' | 'AGENT'; id: string } | null>
selfFixApprovalFloor(projectSlug: string, ref: string, principal: KodaPrincipal): Promise<'agent' | undefined>
```
Use the existing loadTicket/findByRef tenancy and soft-delete semantics; repository unit mocks gain findLatestStatusChangeActor. The new DB spec is apps/api/test/integration/tickets/ticket-latest-status-actor.integration.spec.ts.

[integration] findLatestStatusChangeActor(ticketId, 'VERIFY_FIX') returns null when the ticket has no STATUS_CHANGE row to VERIFY_FIX.

[unit] In that matching-agent case, selfFixApprovalFloor calls findLatestStatusChangeActor exactly once with the ticket's id and 'VERIFY_FIX'.
[unit] For the same ticket with latest actor { type: 'AGENT', id: 'agent-2' }, selfFixApprovalFloor returns undefined.
[unit] For the same ticket and agent principal agent-1 with latest actor { type: 'USER', id: 'agent-1' }, selfFixApprovalFloor returns undefined.
[unit] For a user principal u-1 and latest actor { type: 'USER', id: 'u-1' } on the VERIFY_FIX ticket, selfFixApprovalFloor returns 'agent'.
[unit] For the same VERIFY_FIX ticket with latest actor null, selfFixApprovalFloor returns undefined.
[unit] For an IN_PROGRESS ticket, selfFixApprovalFloor returns undefined.
[unit] For an IN_PROGRESS ticket, selfFixApprovalFloor never calls findLatestStatusChangeActor.
[unit] For a ref with no ticket in the project, selfFixApprovalFloor rejects with NotFoundAppException, as findByRef does.

When the latest matching row has neither actorAgentId nor actorUserId, findLatestStatusChangeActor returns null instead of an earlier actor.

userStories.title: Verify-fix, verify and close apply the self-fix floor
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Prevent an agent from immediately approving, verifying or closing its own fix through any of the three closing REST paths.

**Motivation** — `TicketsController.verifyFix` opens the gate under `ticket.transition.verify-fix.approve` with no reference to who submitted the fix.

**Approach** — `TicketsController.verifyFix` (only when `approve` is true), `verify` and `close` call `selfFixApprovalFloor(slug, ref, principal)` before the gate. When it answers `'agent'`, their `routeGate.run` call carries `minMode: 'agent'`; otherwise the call has no `minMode` property. The return branch of `verifyFix` (`approve` false) does not call it. `PATCH /tickets/:ref` needs no floor: through PATCH only the comment-less edges CREATED/VERIFIED -> IN_PROGRESS succeed, and none of them leaves VERIFY_FIX.

**Scope** — In: three controller entry points, default-undefined service mock, exact gate-call assertions and existing HTTP review-route integration suite. Out: the floor lookup itself (US-002), generic gate behavior (US-001), after-commit workflow effects (US-006). `ticket.transition.verify-fix.return` by the fix's own actor is not given a floor; the design names only the approving edge, and returning a ticket to IN_PROGRESS closes nothing.

**Interface** — Consume `selfFixApprovalFloor(projectSlug: string, ref: string, principal: KodaPrincipal): Promise<'agent' | undefined>` and `minMode?: ApprovalMode` on RouteGateCall. Preserve `TICKET_ROUTE_VARIANTS.verifyFix = 'rest:tickets.verify-fix'`, `.verify`, `.close`, existing comment validation, selected keys and inputs. Approve includes the existing boolean true and string 'true' parsing. Existing review-route cases retain root-authored fixes. New self-agent cases must create the fix through the real /fix route as the calling agent, with no approval policies; the distinct-agent regression uses another agent's fix, and the root self-fix regression submits /fix as root before root approves.

userStories.title: Credential writes are high risk and a CI token rotation needs agent mode
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Require the default agent approval tier for secret-returning credential writes and a contextual agent minimum for CI webhook secret patches.

**Motivation** — An agent bound to global Admin (one human-approved binding) rotates another agent's key with `POST /agents/:slug/rotate-key`, receives the raw key, and impersonates that agent, with `satisfiedBy: none` in the audit.

**Approach** — Credential keys: `catalog.ts` exports `CREDENTIAL_KEYS: ReadonlySet<string>` = `{'agent.create', 'agent.key.rotate', 'user.create'}`. `classifyRisk` answers `'high'` for them, after the critical and read checks and before the `'medium'` fallback. `buildEntry` is unchanged, so their `approval.default` becomes `'agent'` and their floor stays `'none'`.

CI token floor: `ProjectsController.update`, when the parsed patch carries `ciWebhookToken` (any present value, `null` included: clearing the secret is a credential write too, and the route already routes a present value, `!== undefined`, to the redeem variant), adds `minMode: 'agent'` to its `routeGate.run` call (variant `rest:projects.update-ci-token`, redeem header unchanged). A patch without it is unchanged.

**Scope** — In: the three-key risk set, catalog risk oracle and per-key regressions, conditional project route floor, controller exact-shape tests and the existing project CI-token and agent-key HTTP suites. Out: generic minMode mechanics (US-001), Owner-disable checks (US-005), token mint freshness (US-008 through US-010). `agent.update`, `agent.capabilities.update` and `user.update` keep their medium tier. No web, CLI or MCP copy is added for the new 202 answers beyond the feature's API i18n work.

**Interface** — Export `CREDENTIAL_KEYS: ReadonlySet<string>` with exactly `{'agent.create', 'agent.key.rotate', 'user.create'}`; consume `minMode?: ApprovalMode` on RouteGateCall. Preserve `PROJECT_ROUTE_VARIANTS.updateCiToken = 'rest:projects.update-ci-token'`. Update catalog.spec.ts's independent expectedRisk rule after its read check, ProjectsController's exact mixed-secret-patch argument, and the insecure FM-1 immediate-token integration expectation. Existing explicit approval policies and redeem/redaction paths stay in force; a parked credential write must not create its target or return a raw secret.

userStories.title: Only an Owner can disable an Owner
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Refuse a newly disabling Owner patch unless the acting principal also holds the global Owner binding permission.

**Motivation** — `UsersAdminService.update` refuses only a self-disable and the last active admin.

**Approach** — `UsersAdminService.update(actor: PrincipalRef, userId, patch)` replaces the `actorId: string` parameter; `UsersAdminService` gains `PermissionService` as a constructor dependency. Order inside `update`:
1. self-disable refusal (`users.self`), unchanged, comparing `actor.id`;
2. inside the transaction, after the target lookup (`users` 404 unchanged): when `patch.disabled === true` and the target is not already disabled, read `effectiveKeys({ type: 'USER', id: userId }, 'global')`; if it holds `role.binding.owner`, read `effectiveKeys(actor, 'global')`; if that does not hold `role.binding.owner`, throw `new ForbiddenAppException({}, 'users.owner')` (HTTP 403) before any write;
3. the last-admin guard (`users.lastAdmin`), unchanged.
`UserRouteCommands`' `user.update` command passes `{ type: principal.actorType === 'agent' ? 'AGENT' : 'USER', id: principal.id }`. New i18n key `users.owner.40003`: en "Only an Owner can disable an Owner", zh "只有所有者可以停用所有者".

**Scope** — In: service actor contract, PermissionService injection and ordered transaction check, route-command mapping, English/Chinese API i18n, and existing service/command/admin-user tests. Out: credential-key re-tiering (US-004), ticket approval paths (US-001 through US-003). `user.update` other than the Owner rule is not re-tiered; only `disabled` is patchable and the Owner rule covers the reported abuse. No web, CLI or MCP copy is added for the `users.owner` refusal beyond the API i18n key.

**Interface**
```typescript
update(actor: PrincipalRef, userId: string, patch: UpdateUserDto): Promise<UserAdminDto>
```
Read `PermissionService.effectiveKeys(principal: PrincipalRef, scope: PermissionScope): Promise<ReadonlySet<string>>` and `OWNER_BINDING_KEY = 'role.binding.owner'`. Preserve self-disable-first ordering, administration locking, target 404s, token-version and cache invalidation behavior for successful writes. Update every service-test call to PrincipalRef and add an effectiveKeys mock returning an empty set by default. In the existing mutual-disable concurrency test grant Eve global owner rather than admin, keeping its [200,409] result and lock assertions; add Owner protection cases separately.

userStories.title: Transition PR creation and RAG indexing run after commit
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Defer VERIFIED PR creation and CLOSED RAG indexing until the owning transaction commits and suppress classic PR creation when a PR link already exists.

**Motivation** — A settle failure rolls the transition back but leaves the PR, and the stale-approved retry opens a second one.

**Approach** — `TicketTransitionsService` gains `AfterCommitService` as a required constructor dependency, placed right after `audit`. A private helper runs a task after commit: `if (!this.afterCommit.defer(task)) await task();`. Both `createPrForTicket` (VERIFIED) and `autoIndexTicket` (CLOSED, in both places it is called today) go through it. The PR task uses the helper as written. The index task returns the index promise chain (still catching and logging its own failure), is deferred the same way, and when no scope is open is started without being awaited (`void task()`), so the immediate path's response does not wait on the embedding call, as today. On the deferred approval path `executeOnce` already wraps its transaction in `afterCommit.scope`, so the task runs after commit and is dropped on rollback; on the immediate path no scope is open, so the task runs right after the transition's own transaction, as today. `createPrForTicket` also checks `ITicketRepository.hasPrLink(ticketId)` (any `TicketLink` with `linkType: 'pr'`, any source) right after the fleet-ownership check, inside its own try/catch: true returns before any provider call, and a thrown lookup logs a warning and also returns before any provider call (fail closed: no possible duplicate).

**Scope** — In: required constructor injection, both CLOSED index call sites, VERIFIED PR scheduling, any-source PR-link repository query, all affected positional constructors and Nest test providers, and public ApprovalExecutionService.execute composition tests. Out: minimum-mode gate changes (US-001), self-fix controller behavior (US-003), review-decision provenance (US-007). Invite emails sent from a deferred `invite.create` redeem keep their current ordering; the invite keys are critical (human floor) since #381, and moving the send after commit would change the `emailed` flag the redeem answers. The after-commit tasks are best-effort and in-process, as `committedEffect` is: a crash between commit and the PR call loses that PR, as a crash does on the immediate path today. No outbox is added.

**Interface** — `ITicketRepository` gains `hasPrLink(ticketId: string): Promise<boolean>`. Target constructor order: `(ticketRepo, txManager, permissions, audit, afterCommit: AfterCommitService, ragService?, ...the same optional dependencies in the same order)`. Use existing `AfterCommitService.defer(task): boolean` and `scope(fn)`. Implement hasPrLink with one count on TicketLink where linkType is 'pr'. Preserve catching/logging inside PR and index tasks so external failure cannot undo the committed transition. Add apps/api/test/integration/tickets/ticket-pr-link.integration.spec.ts. Positional constructors, mocked ticketLink.count defaults, and direct DI test providers listed in modifiedFiles must be updated together with the implementation; use real AfterCommitService instances in scope tests. Preserve the existing TransitionResult response envelope: verify resolves a result containing ticket, not a bare TicketResponseDto. PR-path fixtures use a CREATED ticket with configured VCS dependencies and no fleet ownership or prior PR link unless the case explicitly tests that guard; verify on a VERIFY_FIX ticket still follows its existing CLOSED path.

userStories.title: A review decision's approver is verified against the thread
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Credit a forge-human approver only when a repository writer is confirmed as an author in the named review thread on the same PR and repository.

**Motivation** — `disagreedBy` comes from an artifact the runner uploads from a raw job's workspace, and the K2 design says these logins are "unverified forge logins; consumers must check artifact trust and commenter permissions".

**Approach** — Review thread lookup: `GitHubAppClient.mintThreadReadToken(installationId, repoName)` mints a token scoped `{ contents: 'read', pull_requests: 'read', metadata: 'read' }` through the existing `mintScopedToken`. `GitHubAppClient.getReviewThread(token, threadId): Promise<ReviewThreadInfo | null>`, `ReviewThreadInfo = { repoOwner: string; repoName: string; prNumber: number; authors: readonly string[] }`. It POSTs `{ query, variables: { id: threadId } }` to the GraphQL endpoint with the bearer token. The endpoint is `<githubApiUrl>/graphql`, except that a `githubApiUrl` ending in `/api/v3` maps to the same host's `/api/graphql`. The query is `query($id: ID!) { node(id: $id) { ... on PullRequestReviewThread { pullRequest { number repository { name owner { login } } } comments(first: 100) { nodes { author { login } } } } } }`. A 200 whose `data` is absent, or whose `data.node` is null or has no `pullRequest`, answers `null` (a `threadId` that is not a review-thread node id lands here). Any non-200 throws `RepoCheckException('provider_error')`. `authors` lists each non-null `author.login`, in order, without duplicates.

Verified approver: `ReviewEventMinter.mintOne` mints its token with `mintThreadReadToken` instead of `mintReadOnlyToken`. It keeps one `getRepoRole` call per non-bot login, as today, but collects every writer (`admin`/`maintain`/`write`) in `disagreedBy` order instead of stopping at the first; a role-check error keeps today's `permission-check-failed` skip. With no writer it skips `no-writer` as today and makes no thread call. With writers, it calls `getReviewThread(token, row.threadId)` exactly once. The thread matches when its `prNumber` equals `row.prNumber` and its `repoOwner`/`repoName` equal the repo's (case-insensitive). The approver is the first writer whose login is among the thread's `authors` (case-insensitive) when the thread matches; the mint then runs under `{ requiredMode: 'human', satisfiedBy: 'human', approverType: 'FORGE_USER', approverId: 'github:<login>' }`. In every other case (no writer among the authors, a null thread, a thread for another PR or repo, or a thrown lookup) the approver is the first writer and the mint runs under the same object with `satisfiedBy: 'none'`. `ReviewDecisionWriter.mint`'s audit summary ends `approver github:<login> (verified thread author)` when the context's `satisfiedBy` is `'human'` and `approver github:<login> (unverified)` otherwise, replacing the fixed "(one of the thread's commenters)" text.

**Scope** — In: a distinct thread-read token, bounded one-call GitHub GraphQL lookup, verified/unverified mint context, writer audit wording and affected unit/integration regressions. Out: fresh runner forge tokens and broker cache bypass (US-008 through US-010). An unverified review decision (`satisfiedBy: 'none'`) is still an active memory decision that later reviews consume; only its audit provenance differs. This is the ruling-14 choice (downgrade, not drop). Existing review decisions minted before this change keep their recorded approval; nothing is re-verified. "Verified" in ruling 14 means the writer authored a comment in the review thread that the event's `threadId` names, on the same PR and repo. It does not prove that this comment is the disagreement, or that the runner-supplied `threadId` belongs to this finding; tying a decision to a specific comment needs nax to report comment ids and is not part of this bundle. US-007 only: `FleetReviewEvent.approverLogin` keeps recording the chosen login for an unverified mint as well; the verified/unverified distinction lives in the action approval (`satisfiedBy`) and the audit summary. US-007 only: GitLab review threads are not looked up; review decisions are GitHub-only today. US-007 only: a thread with more than 100 comments is judged on its first 100 authors. US-007 only: role checks stay one `getRepoRole` call per non-bot login, as today; ruling 14's "one call per event" is the thread lookup.

userStories.title: The API honours a fresh token request for FIX and REVIEW
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Preserve a validated fresh-token wire flag and bypass token reuse only for held FIX/REVIEW job requests.

**Motivation** — The API reuses a cached installation token until `gitTokenReuseMarginSec` (300 s) before it expires, and the runner's `TokenCache` refreshes only inside its own margin, so `CredentialBroker.currentToken(job)` can hand nax a token with 5 to 60 minutes left.

**Approach** — `TokenRequest` (`packages/fleet-protocol/src/index.ts`, types only) gains `fresh?: true`. `parseTokenRequest` accepts `fresh: true` (kept), `fresh: false` (dropped) and refuses any other present value with the parser's `tokenRequest` validation error. `SyncService.grantTokens` forwards `fresh: true` to `GitTokenBroker.mint` only for a request that carries it and whose job is `FIX` or `REVIEW`. `GitTokenBroker.mint`'s request gains `fresh?: boolean`: when true it skips the cache reuse check, mints through the existing `fresh()` path (for `purpose: 'fix'` that path ends in `mintInstallationToken`; for `'review'`, in `mintReviewToken`), and replaces the cache entry under the same key.

**Scope** — In: the explicitly authorized types-only protocol package change despite this story's binding apps/api workdir, strict parser behavior, fenced sync forwarding, purpose-aware cache bypass and existing parser/sync/broker unit specs. Out: producing the runner flag (US-009), waiting and file writers (US-010), thread-read token scopes (US-007). The runner-sync integration suite gains no fresh-token case; the parser, sync and broker units cover it, and the live check exercises it end to end. Deployment is API before runner with no protocol version bump or compatibility fallback.

**Interface** — `TokenRequest` target: `{ jobId: string; leaseEpoch: number; repoId?: string; fresh?: true }`. `GitTokenBroker.mint` request gains `fresh?: boolean`. API imports from @nathapp/fleet-protocol remain type-only. Preserve exact missing-fresh request shapes, existing cache keys and error mapping, default-branch protection checks for FIX, reviewer-specific mint permissions, runnerId/leaseEpoch/state fences and minting outside the sync transaction. A fresh request on any job other than FIX/REVIEW is ignored and may reuse the broker cache.

userStories.title: The runner token cache asks for a fresh token
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add per-job minimum token lifetime demand and retain its fresh flag through the runner's final sync-body reconstruction.

**Motivation** — nax reads `forge-token` once at startup and uses it for every forge call and the push.

**Approach** — `TokenCache.requireFresh(jobId, leaseEpoch, minRemainingMs)` records a minimum remaining life on the job's repo-less entry (creating a wanted entry when there is none), clears that entry's stored error, and calls the `onNeed` listeners. `minRemainingMs` 0 clears the minimum. `requests(nowMs)` composes the two thresholds as: a request is due when the entry is outside its cool-down and its token is missing or has less than `max(refreshMarginMs, minRemainingMs)` left; the request carries `fresh: true` only when `minRemainingMs > 0` and the token is missing or has less than `minRemainingMs` left. `apply` clears the minimum once it stores a token with at least that much left; a token still short of it starts the cool-down. `TokenCache.error(jobId, leaseEpoch, repoId?)` answers the entry's stored error even while a live token is cached (`state()` keeps hiding it then, unchanged). `buildSyncRequest` (`apps/runner/src/sync/batch.ts`), which rebuilds each token request for the wire, forwards `fresh: true` when the request carries it and adds no `fresh` key otherwise; today it copies only `jobId`, `leaseEpoch` and `repoId`.

**Scope** — In: in-memory minimum tracking, requireFresh/error methods, request/cooldown/apply behavior, final wire forwarding and existing cache/batch unit specs. Out: API parsing/cache bypass (US-008), broker polling and forge-token writers (US-010). A token request for a repo-scoped entry (`repoId`) never carries `fresh`; only the job's own token is written to `forge-token`. No new network client or daemon transport is introduced.

**Interface**
```typescript
requireFresh(jobId: string, leaseEpoch: number, minRemainingMs: number): void
error(jobId: string, leaseEpoch: number, repoId?: string): string | null
```
Use upstream `TokenRequest = { jobId: string; leaseEpoch: number; repoId?: string; fresh?: true }`. Preserve highest-epoch selection per job/repo scope, repo-less priority, the 64-request cap, response-to-request epoch correlation and state()'s live-token preference. Keep the existing exact-shape batch assertion for a request without fresh. Normal refresh boundary regressions must remain unchanged; the new minimum is satisfied by at least minRemainingMs remaining.

userStories.title: FIX and REVIEW write a forge token with at least 50 minutes left
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Await a token with at least 50 minutes remaining before each REVIEW/FIX nax step writes its forge-token file.

**Motivation** — The user ruled on 2026-11-02 for a koda-only fresh mint; a generic nax token-refresh command is a later, separate nax feature.

**Approach** — `CredentialBroker.freshToken(job, minRemainingMs, isCancelled?)` calls `requireFresh`, then polls like `firstToken` (same `waitMs`/`pollMs`) and answers `{ ok: true, token }` once the live token has at least `minRemainingMs` left, `{ ok: false, reason: 'git token: <error>' }` as soon as `tokens.error(...)` is set, `{ ok: false, reason: 'git token: timeout' }` at the deadline and `{ ok: false, reason: 'cancelled' }` when cancelled; before it returns, on success and on every refusal, it calls `requireFresh(jobId, leaseEpoch, 0)`, so no stale minimum keeps asking for fresh mints. `CredentialProvider` gains the optional `freshToken`. `HostExecutor` exports `FORGE_TOKEN_MIN_REMAINING_MS = 3_000_000` (50 minutes). Both places that write `forge-token` (`reviewEnv`, used by the REVIEW spawn and by the FIX job's review step, and `spawnFixStep`, the FIX job's fix step) call `freshToken(job, FORGE_TOKEN_MIN_REMAINING_MS)` instead of `currentToken`, throw `new Error(reason)` on a refusal before writing the file, and throw `new Error('git token: none')` when the provider has no `freshToken`.

**Scope** — In: broker polling over the real token cache, optional shared credential seam, exported lifetime constant, both forge-token writer locations and all affected injected providers/test cases. Out: cache/wire request production (US-009), API fresh mint support (US-008), review provenance (US-007). A generic nax forge-token refresh command is not part of this bundle. API deploys before runner; no old-API fallback is added.

Preserve currentToken and existing git/socket consumers, but never fall back to currentToken in REVIEW/FIX writers. Preserve mode-0600 forge-token handling, path-only NAX_FORGE_TOKEN_FILE, deletion at spawn failure/cleanup/attempt wipe and no token logging, argv exposure or journal persistence.
